about.title: Dynalytics
about.tagline: A framework for the rigorous analytics of dynamical systems.
about.lead: Dynalytics is an overarching framework and methodological ecosystem for the analysis and rigorous validation of the dynamics of dynamical systems. It encompasses a diverse family of models — transition networks, co-occurrence networks, psychological networks, and higher-order networks — unified by a single philosophy of scientific rigour. The R, Python, and JavaScript libraries catalogued here are its software layer.
about.more: What sets Dynalytics apart is that analysis and validation are inseparable. A multi-level confirmatory testing battery validates every supported model and every analytical claim: split-half reliability for internal consistency, bootstrapping for edge-level stability, case-dropping for centrality stability, and permutation-based comparisons for groups, conditions, and temporal phases. Where most methods stop at describing a pattern, Dynalytics asks whether that pattern would survive rigorous statistical scrutiny — and supplies the tools to find out.
about.closing: The conceptual groundwork applies to any network or process derived from observed interactions, sequences, or co-occurrence: social, behavioural, cognitive. Its value is not a single technique but a unified theoretical and methodological language for describing change and stability in any dynamic system.
about.peopleIntro: The researchers who build and maintain the Dynalytics toolkit across University of Eastern Finland, FernUniversität in Hagen, and University of Melbourne.

points.t: Every analytical claim must be matched by evidence appropriate to the structure, scope, and complexity of the inference being made — the complexity of the evidence must match the complexity of the claim.

Transition networks (TNA, FTNA, ATNA), co-occurrence networks (CNA, WTNA), heterogeneous (HTNA) and multilayer (MCML) networks, psychological networks, and higher-order networks (HON) — each named for the structure it estimates.

Split-half reliability for internal consistency, bootstrapping for edge stability, case-dropping for centrality stability, and permutation tests for group comparison — so findings reflect genuine system behaviour, not noise or chance.
Implemented across open-source R, Python, and JavaScript libraries plus web and desktop applications — the packages indexed below.

entries.title: tna — Transition Network Analysis (TNA)
entries.blurb: Provides tools for performing Transition Network Analysis (TNA) to study relational dynamics, including functions for building and plotting TNA models, calculating centrality measures, and identifying dominant events and patterns. TNA statistical techniques (e.g., bootstrapping and permutation tests) ensure the reliability of observed insights and confirm that identified dynamics are meaningful.

entries.title: htna — Heterogeneous Transition Network Analysis
entries.blurb: Implements the Heterogeneous Transition Network Analysis (HTNA) method described by López-Pernas et al. (2026). The method is an extension of transition network analysis (TNA) where actions or events belong to two or more distinct actor types (e.g. Human and AI),preserving the actor type partition on the resulting network. Provides a thin, focused API on top of the 'Nestimate' estimation engine and the 'cograph' rendering engine, so downstream bootstrap, permutation, reliability, centrality, and plotting functions treat each actor's codes as a distinct node group.

entries.title: Nestimate — Dynamic, Probabilistic, and Higher-Order Network Analysis
entries.blurb: Estimate, compare, and analyze dynamic and psychological networks using a unified interface. Provides transition network analysis estimation (transition, frequency, co-occurrence, attention-weighted) Saqr et al. (2025), psychological network methods (correlation, partial correlation, 'graphical lasso', 'Ising') Saqr, Beck, and Lopez-Pernas (2024), and higher-order network methods including higher-order networks, higher-order network embedding, hyper-path anomaly, and multi-order generative model. Supports bootstrap inference, permutation testing, split-half reliability, centrality stability analysis, mixed Markov models, multi-cluster multi-layer networks and clustering.

entries.title: cooccure — Co-Occurrence Network Construction and Manipulation
entries.blurb: Constructs co-occurrence networks from several types of input data, such as delimited fields, long/bipartite tables, binary matrices, or wide sequences. Returns tidy edge data frames and supports optional scaling, splitting into several networks, thresholding, and subsetting. Provides eight similarity measures, including Jaccard, cosine, and association strength. Supports export to several network and file formats. Network construction and analysis methods follow Saqr, Lopez-Pernas, Conde, and Hernandez-Garcia (2024, ).

entries.title: bibnets — Importing, Constructing, and Exporting Bibliometric Networks
entries.blurb: Imports, constructs, and exports bibliometric networks from scholarly metadata. Reads 'Scopus', 'Web of Science', 'BibTeX', 'RIS', 'OpenAlex', 'Lens.org', 'Dimensions', and 'Crossref' exports. Goes beyond standard co-networks with attention-weighted networks (lead, last, proximity, circular position weights), position-aware counting (harmonic, arithmetic, geometric, golden-ratio), similarity and dissimilarity normalisations, temporal networks with fixed, sliding, and cumulative windows, disparity-filter backbone extraction, historiograph construction, and local citation scoring. Methods described in López-Pernas, Saqr & Apiola (2023).

entries.title: transitiontrees — Transition Trajectories and Dynamics of Variable-Length Pathways or Sequences
entries.blurb: Analyzes transition trajectories in event, sequence, and ordered data, focusing on how states follow one another, how far processes unfold, and where pathways branch or converge. Trajectories are modeled using variable-order prediction suffix trees, implemented in both frequency-based and prediction-based forms. The framework includes multiple pruning, validation, and smoothing techniques to ensure model robustness. Visualization options include transition trees, radial sunburst diagrams, transition heatmaps, and forward trajectory trees.

entries.title: lagdynamics — Lag Sequential Analysis, Dynamics, and Lag Transition Networks
entries.blurb: A modern, tidy toolkit for lag sequential analysis and lag transition networks of categorical event and sequence data. It provides an accessible, unified workflow for fitting, inspecting, visualising, and comparing lagged transition patterns, with tidy outputs throughout. Includes confirmatory tools for uncertainty, robustness, and group differences, including bootstrap intervals, analytic certainty, split-half reliability, case-drop stability, permutation tests, and Bayesian group comparisons. Supports long-format event-log import, import from common sequence and state-sequence objects, multi-lag analysis, structural-zero constraints, transition and initial probabilities, plotting of transition structures, and a directed transfer-entropy measure. The lag sequential analysis framework follows Sackett and others (1979).

entries.title: litReview — Summarizing Graphs for Literature Reviews
entries.blurb: Summarizes and visualizes categorical data extracted during literature reviews and evidence syntheses, starting from a data frame with one row per study. Generates publication-ready bar, stacked bar, histogram, waffle, donut, treemap, alluvial, trend, co-occurrence, 'UpSet', tree, and study-by-criteria matrix figures, together with world maps and formatted summary tables. Plot functions return standard 'ggplot2' objects that can be further customized, and an interactive 'Shiny' application is included for building figures without writing code. Aims to help researchers report study characteristics consistently across many publications.

entries.title: idiographic — Person-Specific (Idiographic) and Heterogeneous Complex Networks

All estimators are native clean-room implementations. All functions are validated against authoritative literature. Also provides preprocessing audits, edge-stability diagnostics, model-comparison reports, and rolling forecast validation. Methods are described in and.

entries.title: psychnets — Tidy Clean-Room Psychological Network Modeling
entries.blurb: Provides clean-room implementations for estimating psychometric network models, including correlation and partial-correlation networks, Gaussian graphical models with extended Bayesian information criterion (EBIC) regularization, nonparanormal and stepwise selection variants, information-filtering networks (the triangulated maximally filtered graph and the local-global inverse covariance), relative-importance networks, and Ising and mixed graphical models. All methods are implemented from first principles in base R without compiled dependencies and return consistent, tidy outputs. Functions are designed to be transparent and report optimization diagnostics where applicable. For Gaussian graphical models, the graphical lasso stationarity (Karush-Kuhn-Tucker) residual quantifies the deviation of the estimated solution from the optimum of the corresponding convex optimization problem.

entries.title: tsn — Time-Series Network Construction
entries.blurb: Constructs distance, visibility, and state-transition networks from univariate time series. The core constructor provides whole-series and sliding-window distance networks, natural and horizontal visibility graphs following Lacasa et al. (2008) and Luque et al. (2009), and optional state aggregation. Companion verbs expose discretization, trend classification, and an optional bridge to the 'Nestimate' transition-network models. Core network construction uses only packages distributed with R.

entries.title: VaSStra — Simple Variables to States to Sequences to Trajectories
entries.blurb: A small, pipe-friendly implementation of the VaSSTra workflow for longitudinal multivariate data. It provides explicit steps to turn variables into states, states into aligned sequences, and sequences into trajectory groups, followed by tidy trajectory descriptions. A single call runs the complete analysis with transparent, overridable automation of data roles and cluster counts, and an evaluation verb compares the fitted clustering against its alternatives. 'Nestimate' provides the default sequence-clustering backend and all sequence plots. No 'TraMineR' dependency is required.

entries.title: sbert — Sentence Embeddings with 'Sentence-BERT' Models
entries.blurb: Computes sentence embeddings in R without requiring 'Python' by running revision-pinned 'Sentence-BERT' models through 'ONNX Runtime'. Implements model-specific tokenization, attention-mask-aware mean pooling, L2 normalization, cosine similarity, deterministic semantic topic clustering, and class-based term weighting following Reimers and Gurevych (2019). Topic models are evaluated with intrinsic coherence (UMass and normalized pointwise mutual information) and diversity metrics, and summarized with deterministic base-graphics visualizations. Model files are downloaded only after an explicit user request and are stored outside the package library.

entries.title: Ch 14 — Recurrence Quantification Analysis
entries.blurb: Recurrence Quantification Analysis (RQA) is an analytical technique to identify and quantify the repetition, i.e., recurrence, of patterns in nonlinear dynamical systems.

entries.title: Ch 15 — Transition Network Analysis
entries.blurb: As a concept, transition networks were proposed in the seventies by the pioneering work of Schnakenberg.

entries.title: Ch 16 — Frequency-based TNA
entries.blurb: Capturing the dynamics of learning has become an increasingly important goal for educators and researchers due to the value it brings to understanding the learning process.

entries.title: Ch 17 — TNA Clusters
entries.blurb: Clusters, within the context of Transition Network Analysis (TNA), represent distinct subgroups within the sequence data that exhibit unique transition patterns between states or events.

entries.title: Ch 18 — Within-person Analysis
entries.blurb: The last decades of education research witnessed a rapid increase of data availability and advancements in quantitative methods powered by the rise in computing power and methods.

entries.title: Ch 19 — Three Levels of Analysis
entries.blurb: There is an ongoing scientific debate about the best approach to analyze data in order to create effective, personalized recommendations and interventions.

entries.title: Ch 20 — VAR and uSEM
entries.blurb: Network analysis provides a suite of methods for examining both static and dynamic relationships within systems.

entries.title: Ch 21 — Maximum Likelihood Estimator
entries.blurb: People’s cognitive, emotional, motivational, relational, and behavioral patterns emerge from complex, dynamic, and idiosyncratic processes.

entries.title: Ch 22 — Automated Machine Learning
entries.blurb: Predictive analytics is a branch of analytics that uses students’ data, statistical algorithms, or machine learning (ML) techniques to forecast future outcomes;;.

entries.title: Dynalytics: The Birth of a Framework for Rigorous Analytics of Dynamical Systems
entries.blurb: Introduces the Dynalytics framework — a family of models, a multi-level confirmatory testing battery, and the scientific-contract philosophy that ties the ecosystem together.

entries.title: Transition Network Analysis: A Novel Framework for Modeling, Visualizing, and Identifying the Temporal Patterns of Learners and Learning Processes
entries.blurb: The canonical, foundational TNA paper — introduces the framework for modelling, visualising, and identifying the temporal patterns of learners and learning processes.
entries.authors: Saqr, López-Pernas, Törmänen, Kaliisa, Misiejuk & Tikka

entries.title: tna: An R Package for Transition Network Analysis
entries.blurb: The official software paper for the tna R package — cite this when you use the package.

entries.title: Capturing the Process of Students' AI Interactions When Creating and Learning Complex Network Structures
entries.blurb: Captures the process of students' AI interactions while creating and learning complex network structures.

entries.title: The Dynamics of the Self-Regulation Process in Student-AI Interactions: The Case of Problem-Solving in Programming Education
entries.blurb: Models the dynamics of self-regulation in student–AI interactions during programming problem-solving.

entries.title: Cognitive Offloading in Student–AI Collaboration: A Longitudinal Analysis of Prompting Strategies
entries.blurb: A longitudinal analysis of prompting strategies and cognitive offloading in student–AI collaboration.

entries.title: Frequency Transition Network Analysis (FTNA)
entries.blurb: Introduces Frequency Transition Network Analysis (FTNA) — modelling observed transition frequencies directly, without Markov assumptions.
entries.authors: Saqr, Misiejuk, Törmänen, Kaliisa, Tikka & López-Pernas

entries.title: JTNA: A Desktop Software for Transition Network Analysis
entries.blurb: A point-and-click desktop (jamovi) software bringing Transition Network Analysis to non-programmers.

entries.title: Expanding the Quantitative Ethnography Toolkit with Transition Network Analysis: Exploring Methodological Synergies and Boundaries
entries.blurb: Brings Transition Network Analysis into the Quantitative Ethnography toolkit — methodological synergies and boundaries.

entries.title: Role Dynamics in Student-AI Collaboration: A Heterogeneous Transition Network Analysis Approach
entries.blurb: Uses heterogeneous TNA to model role dynamics in student–AI collaboration.

entries.title: Modeling the Dynamics and Impact of Human-AI Interactions with Attention Transition Network Analysis
entries.blurb: Applies Attention Transition Network Analysis (ATNA) to the dynamics and impact of human–AI interactions.

entries.title: Human-AI Collaboration or Obedient and Often Clueless AI in Instruct, Serve, Repeat Dynamics?
entries.blurb: A critical examination of human–AI collaboration and the 'instruct, serve, repeat' dynamic.

entries.title: How AI-Generated Feedback Hinders or Helps Learning: A Heterogeneous TNA Study of Learning Dynamics
entries.blurb: A heterogeneous TNA of how first-grade students engage with real-time AI feedback on multimodal mathematics tasks — when it supports learning and when it gets in the way.

entries.title: Unpacking Vibe Coding: Help-Seeking Processes in Student–AI Interactions While Programming
entries.blurb: A Heterogeneous TNA of 19,418 interaction turns from 110 undergraduates, framing AI-assisted 'vibe coding' as help-seeking — top performers pursue instrumental inquiry that elicits tutor-like responses, while low performers fall into more passive patterns.
entries.authors: Rinja, Oliveira, López-Pernas, Saqr, Specht & Misiejuk

entries.title: tnapy — Transition Network Analysis for Python
entries.blurb: A Python implementation of Transition Network Analysis for users working outside the R ecosystem.

entries.title: JTNA — Transition Network Analysis in jamovi
entries.blurb: A point-and-click jamovi module for TNA: build, plot, and statistically test transition networks with no code.

entries.title: Dynalytics — interactive web app
entries.blurb: A browser-based Shiny application for the Dynalytics framework — run the analyses in the browser, no installation required.

entries.title: TNA — interactive web app
entries.blurb: A browser-based Shiny application for Transition Network Analysis.

entries.title: Vol 1 — LA Methods & Tutorials
entries.blurb: Learning Analytics Methods and Tutorials: a practical guide using R — data, statistics, visualization, clustering, sequence analysis, and networks.

entries.title: Vol 2 — Advanced LA Methods
entries.blurb: Advanced Learning Analytics Methods: AI and explainable AI, LLMs and NLP, complex systems, and advanced transition network analysis.

entries.title: TNA 2026 proceedings published by Springer
entries.blurb: Innovations in Analytics of Learning Dynamics — the proceedings of the First International Workshop on Transition Network Analysis, held in Bergen, Norway on 27 April 2026 — is out in Springer's Communications in Computer and Information Science series, and is open access. Fourteen papers span person-specific and heterogeneous TNA, student–AI interaction dynamics, co-occurrence networks, change-point and period segmentation, and the Dynalytics framework itself. Edited by Mohammed Saqr, Kamila Misiejuk and Sonsoles López-Pernas.

entries.title: litReview is on CRAN
entries.blurb: Summarising graphs for literature reviews and evidence syntheses. Starting from one row per study, litReview builds publication-ready bar, stacked bar, histogram, waffle, donut, treemap, alluvial, trend, co-occurrence, UpSet, tree, and study-by-criteria matrix figures, plus world maps and formatted summary tables. Every plot is a plain ggplot2 object, and a Shiny app builds figures without writing code.

entries.title: idiographic is on CRAN
entries.blurb: Person-specific and within-person network estimation from intensive longitudinal data. One consistent interface covers ordinary VAR, graphical VAR, multilevel VAR, native Bayesian mlVAR/VAR matching Mplus DSEM, unified SEM, GIMME, and rolling networks — with preprocessing and detrending built in, and a clean-room base-R implementation throughout.

entries.title: psychnets is on CRAN
entries.blurb: Tidy, clean-room psychological network modelling in base R. Gaussian graphical models with a full model-selection battery, Ising networks, mixed graphical models, relative importance networks, information-filtering networks, and group networks from event data — each returning tidy results that plot straight through cograph.

entries.title: lagdynamics: modern lag sequential analysis
entries.blurb: A tidy, pipe-friendly toolkit for lag sequential analysis of categorical event sequences. A single lsa() constructor fits classical, two-cell, bidirectional, and dominance engines; every result reads through a tidy verb; and a full confirmatory battery — bootstrap, Dirichlet–Multinomial certainty, split-half reliability, case-drop stability, permutation and Bayesian group comparison — quantifies the evidence behind each edge.

entries.title: htna: Heterogeneous Transition Network Analysis in R
entries.blurb: The R package behind the Heterogeneous TNA papers. It models sequences that mix two or more actor groups (e.g. human and AI) within one interaction — a thin API over the Nestimate and cograph engines builds a transition network across the combined sequence while preserving the actor partition, so bootstrap, permutation, reliability, centrality and plotting treat each actor's codes as a distinct node group.

entries.title: Nestimate: one engine for dynamic & psychological networks
entries.blurb: An R package to estimate, compare, and analyse dynamic and psychological networks through a unified interface — transition, frequency, co-occurrence and attention-weighted TNA estimation, psychometric methods (correlation, partial correlation, graphical lasso, Ising), and higher-order network methods — with bootstrap inference, permutation testing, split-half reliability, and centrality-stability analysis.

entries.title: snakeplot: serpentine plots for long timelines
entries.blurb: A new R package for visualising long timelines, extended sequences, and temporally chained survey or experience-sampling data as intuitive serpentine ('snake') plots — with distribution bars, tick-mark plots, inter-item correlation arcs, faceted multi-construct panels, and time-of-day positioning for ecological momentary assessment data.

entries.title: Saqrmisc: miscellaneous tools for data analysis
entries.blurb: A new R package of miscellaneous functions for data processing, statistical analysis, and visualisation — including model-based clustering with MoEClust, comparison plots with built-in statistical testing, and mosaic-plot analysis for categorical variables, wrapped in robust error handling and a friendly interface.

entries.title: Heterogeneous TNA: how AI feedback helps or hinders learning
entries.blurb: Out now in the Journal of Computer Assisted Learning. López-Pernas, Misiejuk & Saqr use Heterogeneous TNA to trace how first-grade students engage with real-time AI feedback while solving multimodal mathematics tasks — showing, process by process, when the feedback supports learning and when it gets in the way.

entries.title: Heterogeneous TNA: unpacking ‘vibe coding’ in student–AI programming
entries.blurb: A new preprint applies Heterogeneous TNA to 19,418 interaction turns from 110 undergraduates, framing AI-assisted ‘vibe coding’ as help-seeking. Top performers engage in instrumental inquiry and exploration that elicits tutor-like AI responses, while low performers fall into more passive patterns — a process-level contrast only the heterogeneous model surfaces.

entries.title: transitiontrees is on CRAN
entries.blurb: Now available from CRAN, transitiontrees analyses how states follow one another and where pathways branch or converge. It models trajectories with variable-order prediction suffix trees — in both frequency- and prediction-based forms — and visualises them as transition trees, radial sunbursts, heatmaps, and forward-trajectory trees.

entries.title: cooccure: co-occurrence networks from any data
entries.blurb: A new R package that builds co-occurrence networks from delimited fields, long/bipartite tables, binary matrices, or wide sequences. It returns tidy edge tables with eight similarity measures — including Jaccard, cosine, and association strength — plus scaling, thresholding, splitting, and multi-format export.

entries.title: bibnets: bibliometric networks in R
entries.blurb: A new R package for importing, constructing, and exporting bibliometric networks — reading Scopus, Web of Science, OpenAlex, Crossref, Lens, Dimensions, BibTeX and RIS exports. It goes beyond standard co-networks with attention-weighted edges, position-aware counting, temporal windows, disparity-filter backbones, and historiographs.

entries.title: The Dynalytics framework paper is out
entries.blurb: The preprint introducing Dynalytics — its family of models, the confirmatory testing battery, and the scientific-contract philosophy — is now available on SSRN.

entries.title: Cognitive offloading in student–AI collaboration
entries.blurb: A longitudinal analysis of prompting strategies and cognitive offloading in student–AI collaboration, published in Computers in Human Behavior Reports.

entries.title: JTNA brings Transition Network Analysis to jamovi
entries.blurb: A point-and-click desktop module puts the full TNA workflow — build, plot, and statistically test transition networks — in the hands of non-programmers.

entries.title: CRETIC funded by the Research Council of Finland
entries.blurb: A new project on optimising clinical reasoning in time-critical scenarios, using learning-analytics methods from the ecosystem.

entries.title: ISILA and IGLUE: two new Erasmus+ projects
entries.blurb: Erasmus+ funding for early-intervention learning analytics (ISILA) and game-based escape-room learning (IGLUE).

entries.title: Transition Network Analysis introduced at LAK ’25
entries.blurb: The foundational TNA paper — a framework for modelling, visualising, and identifying the temporal patterns of learners and learning processes.

entries.title: CarmNote released: portable analysis in a single HTML file
entries.blurb: CarmNote is now available: a family of interactive, reproducible notebooks for transition and social network analysis. Each notebook is a self-contained HTML file that runs locally in a browser—even offline—keeping data, analysis, figures, results, and notes together. The first releases include CarmNote TNA and CarmNote SNA, with guided workflows and complete documentation.
